key_insight: SynCo co-trains a task-synthesizing agent and a reasoning agent with multi-agent reinforcement learning so the training data evolves with model capability instead of becoming too easy or too hard.
engineering_relevance: For applied LLM systems, this offers a practical route to continual self-improvement by automatically refreshing training tasks as the agent gets stronger.
method: Synthesizer generates math tasks from the Reasoner’s current capability state.
Reasoner solves synthesized tasks and receives correctness-based feedback.
Task quality, answer reliability, and teachability rewards update the Synthesizer, creating an iterative feedback loop.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks, where SynCo outperforms a broad set of synthetic-data methods and baselines, with most gains coming from previously unsolved problems.
watch_item: The approach adds extra training complexity and reward-design sensitivity, so stability and compute cost may be concerns when scaling to new domains.
paper_title: SynCo: Data Synthesis Co-Training for Self-Evolving LLMs via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
